comment: Known answers for the dynamic benchmark in app.mjs. We wrote the target, so a perfect score here is `self-measured` and never `measured` — the NodeGoat benchmark is the one that can surprise us. What this benchmark is for is different: it is the only place where a finding is produced by sending a request and reading the answer, so the modules it covers stop being graded on a pattern match. /api/profile/:id is deliberately correct and appears in `must_not_report`.

defects.cause: no Content-Security-Policy header is sent, so any injected markup executes
not_the_cause: an injection; this is the second layer, missing

defects.cause: responses can be sniffed as a type they were not served as
not_the_cause: a wrong Content-Type; the header is simply absent

defects.cause: neither X-Frame-Options nor frame-ancestors is set, so the page can be framed
not_the_cause: the missing CSP as a whole; frame-ancestors is its own directive

defects.cause: full URLs leak to third parties in the Referer header
not_the_cause: HTTPS; the header travels either way

defects.cause: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is * and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true, so any site reads authenticated responses
not_the_cause: the wildcard on its own, which is harmless without credentials

defects.cause: X-Powered-By names the framework and its version on every response
not_the_cause: the framework being out of date; this is the disclosure

defects.cause: the session cookie is set with no Secure, no HttpOnly and no SameSite
not_the_cause: the cookie value being guessable, which is a separate defect this benchmark does not record

defects.cause: the Location header is taken from the next parameter with no allowlist
not_the_cause: an SSRF; the browser makes the request, not the server

defects.cause: a 500 response carries the stack trace, with absolute paths and module versions
not_the_cause: the underlying TypeError, which is a bug and not the security defect

defects.cause: the handler checks that there is a session, never that the session owns the order
not_the_cause: missing authentication; the endpoint returns 401 without a cookie, and the control request proves it
an enumerable identifier, which only decides how fast the data is read, not whether it can be

must_not_report.why: the same shape as the orders handler, one line longer: it compares the session to the object's owner and answers 403. A cross-account check that reports this is matching the shape of the code, not the behaviour of the server.

correct in the harder way: it answers 200 to every account, and returns that account's own messages. A check that reads the status code and stops reports it. Comparing the bodies is what tells the two endpoints apart.
